name: Manual Seed List / User-Curated Phrase Mechanics
license: internal
termsNotes: Created directly by FusionCanvas users or maintainers; no external phrase text should be copied without separate source attribution and review.
technicalNotes: Use as first collector to validate the source and phrase schemas before automating external sources.
notes: Highest-priority source approach. It supports low-risk phrase mechanics, allows explicit provenance, and avoids copying external expression lists. Store only original user-created templates or records whose external origin has been separately cleared.

name: Internal Structural Template Rulebook
license: internal
termsNotes: Original templates generated from generic grammatical and design-layout rules rather than copied expressions.
technicalNotes: Represent rule families and slot schemas in JSON after human review; do not seed from protected slogans or media quotes.
notes: Good first automated source because it focuses on mechanics such as contrast, identity roles, warning label syntax, and faux certification layouts. Requires examples to be original or drawn from already-approved source records.

name: Internal Workplace and Everyday Expression Review Panel
license: internal
termsNotes: Reviewer-created notes and templates are internal; participants should avoid importing exact phrases from copyrighted books, social feeds, merch listings, ads, songs, movies, or TV.
technicalNotes: Collect reviewer suggestions with provenance fields, review status, and duplicate checks before promotion to phrase records.
notes: Useful for current workplace language that public-domain sources cannot cover. Keep manual by default because recognizability and overuse are subjective, and because modern web examples may be rights-unclear.

name: Wiktionary Category: English idioms
license: CC BY-SA 4.0 / GFDL per Wikimedia dump licensing; verify page-level notices before collection
termsNotes: Wikimedia text is reusable including commercially with attribution and share-alike obligations; dumps can contain exceptions or possible unnoticed infringements.
accessMethod: MediaWiki API or Wikimedia XML dumps
technicalNotes: Category is large and semi-structured. Collector should extract entry titles and idiom labels only after confirming attribution/share-alike handling and excluding modern distinctive quotations.
notes: Strong candidate for idioms because entries are categorized and maintained, but not approved for blind collection due to share-alike implications, entry noise, and varying suitability for POD. Store source metadata and review each candidate.

name: Wiktionary Category: English proverbs
license: CC BY-SA 4.0 / GFDL per Wikimedia dump licensing; verify page-level notices before collection
termsNotes: Commercial reuse is generally allowed under Wikimedia licensing, but attribution/share-alike duties and possible exceptions must be handled.
accessMethod: MediaWiki API or Wikimedia XML dumps
technicalNotes: Category pages and entry metadata provide good starting structure; proverb variants and regional forms need normalization and manual deduplication.
notes: Good proverb source with recognizable traditional material, but use manual review before collection because CC BY-SA compliance, proverb variants, and cultural specificity must be tracked.

name: Wiktionary Appendix: English snowclones
license: CC BY-SA 4.0 / GFDL per Wikimedia dump licensing; verify page-level notices before collection
termsNotes: Templates may reference modern movies, ads, songs, or other high-risk origins; exact templates should be legal-risk scored individually.
technicalNotes: Appendix is already template-oriented and easier to review than general phrase lists, but many entries include source-origin notes that should remain metadata only until cleared.
notes: Excellent source for identifying plug-in mechanics, but not safe for direct ingestion because some snowclones are derived from protected or trademark-adjacent pop culture. Use for template review and risk flags.

name: Wikimedia Dumps for English Wiktionary
license: Wikimedia project licenses, generally CC BY-SA 4.0/GFDL for text; confirm project-specific and page-specific terms
termsNotes: Wikimedia dump legal page says content can generally be reused for commercial purposes, but also notes fair-use exceptions and possible unnoticed infringements.
technicalNotes: Best access route for repeatable collectors once licensing and attribution requirements are implemented. Parsing Wiktionary templates can be complex.
notes: Treat as a technical access approach rather than a standalone phrase source. Research later after page-level candidates are approved and attribution/share-alike storage requirements are designed.

name: Project Gutenberg: A Dictionary of English Proverbs and Proverbial Phrases
license: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record
termsNotes: Project Gutenberg trademark/license boilerplate applies to redistribution of Gutenberg-branded files; extract and store only reviewed phrase records with provenance.
accessMethod: downloadable HTML/plain text from Project Gutenberg
technicalNotes: Alphabetical reference work with an index. Parsing may require cleanup, but public-domain status and topical focus are strong.
notes: Priority public-domain proverb source. Because many entries are traditional or archaic, collector should score modern recognizability and design suitability rather than importing everything.

name: Project Gutenberg: Bartlett's Familiar Quotations
license: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record
termsNotes: Although the source is public-domain, it is quote-oriented and may include fixed literary passages; avoid direct storage of long quotations and prioritize phrase/proverb mechanics.
accessMethod: downloadable plain text/HTML from Project Gutenberg
technicalNotes: Structured by source author/work rather than by phrase pattern. Requires substantial filtering for short, traditional, or pattern-like entries.
notes: Useful for recognizing classic proverbial and literary phrase mechanics, but direct phrase collection is lower priority because famous quotations are not in this first pass focus. Manual review only.

name: Project Gutenberg: Moby Word Lists
license: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record
termsNotes: Lexical word and phrase lists are public-domain in the U.S.; verify individual Moby subfiles before relying on specialized lists.
technicalNotes: Better as a slot-filling vocabulary and phrase-normalization aid than as a direct phrase pattern source.
notes: Use for generating safe slot vocabularies, detecting multi-word lexical items, and enriching structural templates. Do not treat it as a curated idiom/proverb source.

name: Project Gutenberg / Public Domain Review: 1811 Dictionary of the Vulgar Tongue
license: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg/Public Domain Review records
termsNotes: Contains historical slang and offensive or obsolete terms; commercial suitability requires careful filtering.
accessMethod: downloadable plain text/HTML from Project Gutenberg; contextual record at Public Domain Review
technicalNotes: Dictionary-like entries are parseable but archaic and noisy. Use sparingly for idiom origins or historical mechanics.
notes: Legally attractive but creatively mixed because much language is obsolete or unsuitable. Manual review only; likely not an early collector.

name: Princeton WordNet
license: WordNet license; free for research and commercial users subject to license and citation requirements
termsNotes: License is clear and permissive but requires compliance and citation; WordNet trademark should be respected.
technicalNotes: Contains lexical entries including some multi-word expressions. Best for normalization, synonym slots, and lexical relations rather than proverb harvesting.
notes: Strong support dataset for slot expansion, noun/verb classing, and idiom-like multiword expressions. It should enrich phrase records rather than drive the main pattern inventory.

name: Open English WordNet
license: Open-source license in repository; verify current LICENSE.md before collection
termsNotes: Fork of Princeton WordNet with ongoing open development; license appears repository-defined and should be pinned to a commit.
technicalNotes: Well-structured graph files; useful for lexical enrichment and slot classes, not as a phrase-content source.
notes: Promising technical source, but verify license file and decide whether Princeton WordNet alone is sufficient before adding another lexical dependency.

name: ConceptNet 5
license: CC BY-SA 4.0
termsNotes: Share-alike obligations are clear but may be awkward for downstream commercial product data. Node/source provenance varies because the graph aggregates multiple resources.
technicalNotes: Can find common-sense relations, related terms, and some natural-language phrases. Use for enrichment and candidate discovery, not direct storage without review.
notes: Useful API/tooling source for slot enrichment and everyday concept relationships. Because of CC BY-SA and mixed provenance, avoid blind phrase ingestion.

name: Datamuse API
license: Service terms/API documentation; verify current terms before production use
termsNotes: API is primarily a word-finding tool, not a phrase corpus license. Use generated word suggestions as tooling support, not source phrase records.
technicalNotes: Helpful for rhymes, related words, constraints, adjectives, and slot-filler suggestions during phrase generation.
notes: Good candidate as an auxiliary API after terms review. It should not be considered an external phrase-content source for this milestone.

name: Google Books Ngram Viewer / Ngram Dataset
license: Dataset/Google terms require separate review before automated use
termsNotes: Good for frequency validation and historical trend checks; not a license to collect phrase content from copyrighted books.
accessMethod: web interface and downloadable n-gram datasets
technicalNotes: Use only to score recognition/frequency of already-approved phrases or templates. Avoid storing newly discovered copyrighted-source snippets.
notes: Valuable validation tool, not a direct phrase source. License and terms are not clear enough for collection in this pass.

name: Berkeley FrameNet
license: FrameNet data license appears non-commercial in some package metadata; verify official current license before use
termsNotes: Because commercial use appears restricted or unclear, use only for research inspiration unless legal review approves a specific data package.
accessMethod: browsable reports and downloadable XML release
technicalNotes: Highly structured semantic frames and valence patterns, but not a POD phrase source and may have non-commercial limitations.
notes: Useful for understanding grammatical frames and argument structures, not for storing phrase records. License risk prevents collection in a commercial product workflow at this stage.

name: VerbNet
license: Requires verification from VerbNet download/license page before production use
termsNotes: Potentially open academic resource, but license clarity for commercial phrase-generation support must be confirmed.
technicalNotes: Useful for verb classes, syntax frames, and slot behavior rather than direct phrase patterns.
notes: Promising structural source, but defer until exact license terms are pinned. Best use would be enriching internally generated linguistic patterns.

name: FHWA Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)
license: U.S. federal government/public domain for traffic control device design/application provisions, with stated exceptions
termsNotes: Avoid copying protected shields, marks, logos, state/local materials, or standardized sign designs too closely for novelty products.
accessMethod: official PDFs/HTML; Wikisource mirrors for reference only
technicalNotes: Use to learn generic sign grammar, signal words, and traffic-control message structure. Do not ingest exact sign legends as product phrases without review.
notes: Good low-risk source for signage mechanics and visual conventions, especially because official traffic sign language is widely recognizable. Keep collection manual to avoid creating confusing official-looking products or copying protected marks.

name: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.145 Accident Prevention Signs and Tags
license: U.S. federal regulation / public domain; verify any incorporated third-party standards separately
termsNotes: The OSHA regulation is public, but ANSI/ISO standards and commercial sign examples are not automatically reusable.
technicalNotes: Useful for generic warning-tag structure and signal-word taxonomy. Avoid claiming compliance or imitating regulated labels in a misleading way.
notes: Strong source for warning-sign structure and faux authority concepts, but it should drive generic templates only. Do not copy ANSI-owned layouts or imply official safety certification.

name: ISO 3864 / ANSI Z535 Safety Sign Standards
license: Copyrighted/proprietary standards; not open for phrase or layout extraction
termsNotes: Standards are sold/licensed by ISO/ANSI/NEMA. Use only high-level awareness; do not copy standard text, symbols, tables, or layouts.
technicalNotes: Technically unsuitable for collection; public summaries can inform legal-risk review of signage patterns.
notes: Important to know what not to copy. Treat as design-risk context only and rely on original parody/generic warning templates or public U.S. government regulations instead.

name: The Snowclones Database
license: No clear reusable content license found in first pass
termsNotes: Independent blog/database with unclear rights; many entries discuss modern pop culture or technology references.
accessMethod: manual browsing only unless permission/license is confirmed
technicalNotes: WordPress-like structure with useful posts, but no collector should be built without permission and legal review.
notes: Excellent conceptual reference for snowclone mechanics, but unclear license makes it unsuitable for storing phrases or scraping. Use only to guide manual creation of original template records.

name: Know Your Meme
license: Unclear/restrictive site content rights; many entries involve copyrighted media, brands, and identifiable creators
termsNotes: Modern memes often have creator, platform, publicity, trademark, or media-franchise risks. Song lyrics, movie/TV quotes, and ad slogans remain out of scope for this pass.
technicalNotes: Useful metadata and cultural history, but not suitable for phrase ingestion or scraping in this phase.
notes: Good trend/context reference but high legal and license uncertainty. Do not store meme phrase content from it; at most use it to identify broad mechanics for separately authored internal templates.

name: Commercial Idiom Websites (The Free Dictionary, UsingEnglish, similar)
license: Unclear or proprietary website content; site terms must be reviewed individually
termsNotes: Do not assume public web lists are safe for commercial reuse. Definitions and example sentences are likely copyrighted site content.
accessMethod: manual browsing only for source comparison
technicalNotes: Often structured and broad, but unsuitable for scraping or direct phrase storage without explicit permission.
notes: Useful as a comparison point to understand idiom coverage, but not an approved source. Prefer Wiktionary, public-domain books, and internal curation instead.

name: Subtitle / Movie-TV Quote Corpora
license: Mixed/unclear; underlying scripts, subtitles, and quotes are typically copyrighted
termsNotes: Movie quotes, TV quotes, and song lyrics are out of scope for this first pass and should not be collected directly.
technicalNotes: Even if technically downloadable, phrase extraction would conflict with current scope and risk posture.
notes: Excluded from the first source pass. This protects the database from distinctive protected media quotes and avoids scope creep into songs, film, TV, and advertising.
